concepts.title: The CSS box model
concepts.summary: Every element is a content box wrapped in padding, border and margin. Layout bugs are usually box-model bugs.
common_errors: Adding width and padding without border-box and overflowing the row
Collapsing margins mistaken for missing margin

concepts.title: Semantic HTML structure
concepts.summary: Document structure carries meaning: headings, landmarks, labels and form controls.

concepts.title: Bootstrap grid and utilities
concepts.summary: A 12-column responsive grid plus utility classes. Composition replaces bespoke CSS for most layouts.
common_errors: Columns not wrapped in a row

concepts.title: Form validation
concepts.summary: Client-side validation is UX. Server-side validation is correctness and security. You need both.

concepts.title: The PHP request lifecycle
concepts.summary: A request arrives, PHP runs top to bottom, produces a response, and forgets everything unless you persist it.

concepts.title: CRUD operations
concepts.summary: Create, read, update, delete — the four operations every transactional site is built from.
common_errors: Reading before checking the insert succeeded

concepts.title: Relational modelling
concepts.summary: Entities become tables, relationships become keys. The ERD is the contract for everything above it.
concepts.code_example: CREATE TABLE bookings (id INT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INT NOT NULL);

concepts.title: Normalisation to 3NF
concepts.summary: Remove repeating groups, partial dependencies and transitive dependencies so a fact lives in exactly one place.
common_errors: Storing customer name on the booking row
Normalising past the point of usefulness

concepts.title: Prepared statements
concepts.summary: Parameterised queries separate code from data, which is what actually stops SQL injection.

concepts.title: Sessions and authentication
concepts.summary: A session is a server-side record keyed by a cookie. Authentication decides who you are; authorisation decides what you may do.
common_errors: Checking auth in the UI only

concepts.title: Test evidence
concepts.summary: A test is a claim plus the observation that supports it. Evidence is what turns a claim into a mark.
common_errors: Screenshots with no expected value stated

concepts.title: Architectural Decision Records
concepts.summary: Context, decision, alternatives, rationale, consequences. Written when the decision is made, not reconstructed at the end.
common_errors: Describing what was built instead of why
Writing all ADRs the night before

decisions.title: Use prepared statements for every database write
decisions.context: The booking form writes user-supplied values straight into MySQL. Early prototypes concatenated the values into the SQL string.
decisions.decision: All reads and writes go through PDO prepared statements with bound parameters.
alternatives: Validate input strictly and keep string concatenation
decisions.rationale: Escaping depends on remembering to escape every value in every place. Binding separates code from data structurally, so the failure mode is a broken query rather than an injection.
consequences: Every query needs a prepare/execute pair, which is more verbose
Dynamic column names still need an allow-list, since they cannot be bound

decisions.title: Relational database architecture for the booking system
decisions.context: Bookings, customers and slots were originally one wide table, which duplicated customer details on every booking.
decisions.decision: Split into customers, slots and bookings, with bookings holding foreign keys to both.
alternatives: Keep one denormalised bookings table for simpler queries
Separate customers only, leaving slot text on the booking
decisions.rationale: Duplicated customer details caused update anomalies during testing: changing an email updated only one row. Third normal form removes the anomaly and makes the ERD legible to the examiner.
consequences: Referential integrity is enforced by the database rather than by application code

decisions.title: Adopt Bootstrap rather than bespoke CSS
decisions.context: The interface needs to be responsive and consistent, but the time budget is dominated by the database and PHP work.
decisions.decision: Use Bootstrap 5 utilities and grid for layout; write custom CSS only for brand colour and spacing overrides.
alternatives: A CSS reset plus custom grid
decisions.rationale: The assessment rewards a working, consistent interface, not novel CSS. Bootstrap makes the box model explicit through named classes, which also gives the learner vocabulary to explain the layout.
consequences: Any bespoke visual identity has to override defaults deliberately

decisions.title: Server-side validation is authoritative
decisions.context: HTML5 validation already blocks empty and malformed fields in the browser.
decisions.decision: Treat client-side validation as a hint and revalidate everything in PHP before persisting.
decisions.rationale: Client-side checks can be bypassed with a crafted request, so they cannot be the guarantee. Revalidating server-side keeps the database the single point of truth for what a valid booking is.
consequences: Validation rules exist in two places and must stay in step

decisions.title: Hash passwords with password_hash rather than a custom scheme
decisions.context: Staff accounts need a login to manage slots.
decisions.decision: Store only password_hash output and verify with password_verify.
decisions.rationale: A hand-rolled scheme has to get salting, iteration count and comparison timing right. password_hash is the language's maintained default and upgrades algorithm over time.
consequences: Hashes are opaque and cannot be compared directly in SQL

decisions.title: Test boundary and erroneous cases, not just valid ones
decisions.context: Initial testing only showed the booking succeeding.
decisions.decision: Every feature gets a normal, boundary and erroneous test case recorded with expected and actual results.
decisions.rationale: Evidence of failure handling is what distinguishes a described system from a tested one, and the boundary cases are where the date and slot logic actually breaks.
consequences: The test table grows substantially and needs maintaining as features change

evidence.body: booking-form.html renders a two-column layout that stacks below the md breakpoint.

Test-024: submitting "' OR 1=1 --" as the name stores the literal string and returns one row.
schema.sql defines customers, slots and bookings with two foreign keys.
Test-031: a POST sent with curl bypassing the browser is rejected with 'Invalid email'.
login.php calls password_verify and regenerates the session id on success.
